inventedEvidence.evidence: 'The stiff and gritty feeling confirms that debris has worked its way past the filter' - customer never said debris was found; filter had only fluff

confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'it is almost certainly the drain pump' and 'You need to replace the pump' without ruling out sump hose blockage

unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'Bosch Drain Pump 00672819' recommended with model unknown

compatibilityWithoutEvidence.evidence: 'Your model FD 9409 likely corresponds to a Bosch WAW series washer' and 'This is the most common drain pump used in Bosch front-load washers from your era, including models like WAW28540GB'

rationale: The assistant never explained that FD 9409 is a production code. It treated it as a model number and repeatedly named pump part number 00672819 with invented compatibility claims (WAW28540GB etc.), even after the customer said the E-Nr was unreadable. It was confident the pump was dead without addressing the sump hose blockage possibility, and it did not suggest an engineer or finding the E-Nr via receipt or registration. It also told the customer to remove the pump after they said they would not go beyond the filter. It did correctly use E18 and the hum, and it advised unplugging first.</br>
